# CANDIDATE: VWAP_CONTINUATION_ANCHOR_VALIDATION

**Filed:** 2026-07-21  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** new_trigger  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

The VWAP_CONTINUATION setup captures directional bias from the first three RTH closes relative to VWAP, providing a morning edge that aligns with J's BEARISH_REJECTION anchor days. We hypothesize that enabling this trigger with standard V15 execution parameters will capture a portion of the anchor day P&L without degrading performance on loser days.

## Mechanism

**Entry:** When the first three RTH closes are all on the same side of the session VWAP (as‑of, no look‑ahead), take the first qualifying bar ≤ 10:30 ET that continues the trend—either a breakout (fresh in‑trend extreme) or a pullback (shallow VWAP‑ward dip then with‑trend close). Enter at the next bar open.  
**Contract selection:** ITM‑2 put for bearish bias (matches anchor days), min 3 contracts, premium target $0.50–$2.00, limit at mid.  
**Exit:** Chart‑stop‑only (session extreme against the trade) as primary stop; catastrophe premium stop −50% (Safe) or −7% bear (Bold) only as backstop; TP1 = +50% premium at qty fraction 0.667 (sell 2 of 3); runner moves to breakeven after TP1 and exits on re‑entry into the EMA ribbon, rejection signature, or premium ≥ entry × 3.0; time stop 15:50 ET.

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** qty=28 requires $25K+ account; $1K paper account approximates 14% of headline P&L (risk per trade capped at 50% of equity, 3‑contract minimum scales to ~28 contracts at $25K).  
2. **Sample bias:** Full history 2025‑01‑02 to 2026‑06‑18 (≈16 months) used for Stage‑1 grinder; risk of overfit mitigated by walk‑forward OOS and concentration checks.  
3. **Out-of-sample:** NEEDS-OOS (walk‑forward held‑out window not yet run).  
4. **Real‑fills:** NEEDS-REAL‑FILLS (real OPRA fill validation not yet performed).  
5. **Failure modes:** Worst day: large adverse gap against trend triggering chart stop; max drawdown: consecutive losing days in choppy regimes; blow‑up scenario: volatility expansion causing repeated premature stops on pullback entries.  
6. **Concentration:** unknown -- requires Stage-1 backtest to compute top‑5‑day % of P&L.
